note: Both sets make the same core error of attributing the R-57.5 table row values (e.g., 17,080 Btu/hr, 2,423 kWh, 2,870 kWh, 3,920 kWh, 15,852 Btu/hr, 2,882 kWh) to R-47.5. Set A nevertheless binds most values to the correct property (heating/cooling load vs. heating/cooling/total energy use) and software (eQuest vs. BEoptE+), so its surviving claims are meaningful and supported, though a few loads are mislabeled as 'energy use'. Set B leaves nearly every attribute as a placeholder ('value 1', 'energy value 2', 'energy analysis result'), so even its correctly valued claims do not identify the measured property, and it also misbinds the R-57.5 rows. Neither set captures the 2.08%/0.51% energy-increase results.
